output.brief: VA-220 failures are coming from Pellacott's 2026-built valves, not from installers or firmware. Brenmoor's quality lab matched claims by serial number. Pellacott valves fail at the same rate (about 41 per 1,000) across old and new installers and across both firmware versions. Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7 per 1,000 everywhere. Un-installed Pellacott 2026 stock leaks at the seat in 11% of samples, against 0–1% for others. The leak-test rig was out of service from 9 Jan 2026. No VA-220 test program was loaded on the other rigs. Certificate tables repeat four fixed sequences, some already present in Nov 2025. So the "100% leak-tested" certificates, which drove the score rise and dock-to-stock status, don't reflect real tests. Don't release the six held lots on fresh paperwork. Don't penalise installers. Next steps: quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and release only after Brenmoor's own helium testing. Then require rig logs or witnessed tests for scoring, and check other suppliers' records. The seal change (Corlin) and the move to Line 3 are confounded. Don't mandate a seal reversion until they are separated. Confidence is high on the main finding. It is lower on the seal as the specific cause, and on whether other suppliers are affected.
